focus: Corrupt/truncated saves recovery and unknown keys

route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged probe_save_recovery completed its isolated save-fixture assertions on exact Godot 4.7.2-stable. It verifies backup creation, unknown-key round trips, truncation and typed/incomplete corruption fallback, field-local preference repair, future-schema protection, defaults for additive keys, and New Game archive restore.
route_status.route_gaps: The probe instantiates ReefMain and writes test save files and damaged JSON directly; it does not open a player-facing Continue route, send touch input, kill/relaunch the real app, or observe recovery feedback. The save system is called by live startup via main.gd:1078 and routed through _write_save at :3296-3311, but those gameplay routes are outside this probe. MA-SAVE-001 remains open for castle interaction scratch progress and is outside this recovery focus.

code_constants.value: The focused probe has no frame waits, timers, or input delays; its fixture setup and checks execute synchronously in _init.
code_constants.scope: Harness execution only; not a gameplay duration.

code_constants.value: Startup calls _load_save directly; failed writes set save_dirty and a 1.5-second retry delay.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: recovering the last complete progress lets a child keep her prior choices after a crash; no child experienced this run.
play_appeal.variety: Not assessed; the probe does not enter a game activity.
play_appeal.world_response: Recovery restores serialized values and repairs a JSON file, but this run does not inspect any visible world response or explanation.
play_appeal.replay: Whether a child wants to return after recovery, or notices a replay loop, is unknown.
play_appeal.appeal_test: On a Lenovo Tab M11 with an isolated test save, have an adult prepare a valid primary/backup pair containing one recognizable completed milestone and an unknown marker, then truncate only the primary and launch. Let the child use the visible Continue control without explanation. Record whether she recognizes the restored room/milestone, chooses to continue for 60 seconds, repeats or abandons the same action, and shows confusion or frustration; then verify the marker and progress survived. Repeat once with a clean save as control. Do not use a child's real save for fault injection.

observations.title: A truncated primary recovers the prior complete save and repairs the primary
evidence: runtime/L49/attempt_1/receipt.json: PASS; exact engine 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf, isolated profile, exit 0, no timeout or failure lines.
runtime/L49/attempt_1/probe.log: truncated primary found clean recovery copy; backup selected; pearls 17 and dungeon progress 4 restored; repaired primary readable.
scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:123-131 writes '{truncated}' and asserts backup selection and repair.
observations.reproduction: The one authorized L49 invocation completed with SAVE_RECOVERY|RESULT: ALL OK; the truncated-primary fixture assertions are logged.
observations.child_impact: This recovery case could protect a child's saved progress after an interrupted write; visible Continue and room restoration were not exercised.
observations.proposed_repair: No code repair indicated for the tested truncated-primary case. Keep the backup recovery path and test user-visible re-entry separately.
observations.acceptance_test: On target device, fault-inject a truncated primary into an isolated test profile with a known-good backup, launch, use visible Continue, and verify last acknowledged progress appears without an extra action or false reward.

observations.title: Unknown save data survives writes and archive restoration
evidence: scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:24-44 seeds and checks future_payload dictionary and future_list array.
scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:163-177 checks a future_only_progress field is preserved byte-for-byte when the older writer refuses a write.
scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:295-325 checks archive_unknown survives New Game archive and restore.
runtime/L49/attempt_1/probe.log: unknown dictionary/array, future save untouched, and archive unknown fields preserved assertions all pass.
observations.reproduction: Run the retained L49 probe command and inspect the named unknown-field assertions; all reported OK.
observations.child_impact: Preserving fields from another build reduces risk of erasing progress this build does not understand; the child-visible impact is indirect and not observed.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair indicated in the covered paths. Continue treating unknown fields as part of the save document during normalization and transactional writes.
observations.acceptance_test: Round-trip unknown dictionary and array markers through write, backup recovery, and archive restore; verify exact values remain while known current-build fields normalize.

observations.title: The probe checks field-local preference repair and avoids demoting newer progress
evidence: scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:151-161 corrupts quality and touch_mode while setting pearls to 44; primary is retained and touch_mode normalizes to Hybrid.
scripts/save_state.gd:431-450 selects clean candidates by save_generation and retains a valid complete primary with clean progress even when a preference needs normalization.
runtime/L49/attempt_1/probe.log: noncritical damage keeps newer primary, pearls 44, invalid touch preference repairs to Hybrid.
observations.reproduction: The exact preference_damage fixture selects TEST_PATH and verifies pearls 44 and touch_mode hybrid; its assertions pass in L49.
observations.child_impact: A damaged preference need not force loss of unrelated progress, but no settings screen or child-facing repair cue was viewed.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair indicated for these tested fields. Retain the distinction between recoverable preference damage and critical progression damage.
observations.acceptance_test: Inject one invalid noncritical preference alongside newer progress and a valid older backup; verify the newest progress remains, the preference defaults safely, and a separate critical-field corruption still recovers the backup.

observations.title: Future schema writes are blocked without letting stale future sidecars disable current saves
evidence: scripts/save_state.gd:227-240 disables write_save when the selected document is future schema and returns false.
scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:163-205 verifies the future primary stays byte-for-byte unchanged, future backup outranks an older clean temp, and a stale future temp does not block a current write.
runtime/L49/attempt_1/probe.log: all named future-schema and stale-future-temp assertions pass.
observations.reproduction: Probe creates future schema and stale-sidecar fixtures; exact primary, candidate and subsequent-write assertions pass.
observations.child_impact: The tested paths avoid silently replacing newer-build data or suppressing current-build saves because of an abandoned temp; the resulting in-memory progress may still be unsaved when writing against a future schema.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair indicated for selection/write protections covered here. Keep the existing save_dirty retry route visible to the caller when writes return false.
observations.acceptance_test: On disposable profiles, test a future primary, future backup plus older temp, and stale future temp beside a current primary; verify preservation, candidate order, reported write failure, and successful current save respectively.

observations.title: Damaged and incomplete saves distinguish critical loss risk from additive defaults
evidence: scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:133-149 verifies wrong-typed pearls and a syntactically valid but incomplete schema save both fall back to the clean backup.
scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:207-230 verifies missing newer-added stickers, critters, and touch_mode default without demoting the primary or losing pearls 12.
runtime/L49/attempt_1/probe.log: wrong known type falls back, incomplete primary falls back, defaults restored, newest progress kept.
observations.reproduction: Run L49; inspect the wrong-type, incomplete, and core-quartet fixtures and their ALL OK log entries.
observations.child_impact: These code paths protect progress across schema growth and critical damage in their fixtures, though no actual legacy family save was opened in the UI.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair indicated for the tested schema cases. Keep new keys defaulted and preserve the frozen core completeness boundary.
observations.acceptance_test: Run a corpus of supported legacy saves and synthetic damaged copies through the player-facing startup path; verify added keys default, valid newer progress wins, and genuinely incomplete/critical saves use the last-known-good backup.

observations.title: The focused recovery probe bypasses player input and app lifecycle routes
evidence: scripts/probe_save_recovery.gd:21-36 constructs ReefMain, seeds state and writes files directly; lines 123-325 mutate fixture files and call SaveState methods without UI input.
scripts/save_state.gd:98-122 loads selected data during startup and restores main state; scripts/main.gd:1078 calls _load_save.
scripts/main.gd:3296-3311 routes writes and retry state through the main game, but those caller behaviors are not driven by this probe.
runtime/L49/attempt_1/receipt.json: headless=true and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false.
observations.reproduction: Read probe setup and fixture sections; no InputEvent, visible Continue tap, pause/focus event, or OS process restart appears in this test path.
observations.child_impact: It remains unknown whether a child can identify the recovery route, whether repaired progress is apparent, and whether touch/device timing feels responsive.
observations.proposed_repair: No source defect inferred. Add a routed device recovery check and observed child comprehension/appeal evidence as separate acceptance lanes.
observations.acceptance_test: On Lenovo Tab M11, trigger a controlled corrupt-primary/clean-backup startup in a disposable profile; let the child reach the resumed activity with touch only, then record taps, wait intervals, visible state, device pacing, and whether she chooses to continue.
